meta.ephemeris: JPL Horizons API: apparent (airless) azimuth/elevation of Sun (10) and Earth (399) from topocentric sites on the Moon (coord@301, geodetic)
meta.terrain: NASA LRO LOLA LDEM_75S_240M (240 m/pixel); 360 one-degree rays to 320 km with lunar curvature; observer 2 m above the surface; sites snapped to the highest terrain within 2.4 km of each candidate coordinate
meta.subsolarNote: hourly [lat, lon] of the sub-solar point from Horizons (observer: Sun centre, target: Moon)
meta.nasaIllum: nasaIllumPct: NASA GSFC PGDA LOLA polar illumination map AVGVISIB_85S_060M_201608 (Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211), average solar-disc visibility over 18.6 years, sampled at each site (60 m/pixel, surface level).

sites.name: Connecting Ridge
sites.summary: A raised ridge joining the rims of Shackleton and de Gerlache craters, almost on the pole itself. Its height lifts it above most nearby shadows, making it one of the best-lit places on the Moon, with permanently shadowed crater floors, where water ice may be trapped, within reach.

sites.name: Peak Near Shackleton
sites.summary: A high point on the far side of Shackleton crater. Being high above the surrounding terrain gives long stretches of sunlight, and the slopes below lead toward the shadowed interior of Shackleton.

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim 1
sites.summary: A high point on the rim of de Gerlache crater. The crater floor below is a permanently shadowed region worth sampling, and the rim itself rises high enough to see the Sun over most of the surrounding terrain.

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.summary: A five-kilometre-high massif about four degrees from the pole, on the side of the Moon that faces Earth. That makes direct-to-Earth radio easier, but being farther from the pole means the Sun swings lower each month and can drop out of view for days at a time.
